end.note: Year precision only: bounded above by the 2023 PRL's statement that SND@LHC recorded pp collision data in 2022; no source consulted gives an exact installation/commissioning-complete date.

intervals.label: approved / construction / commissioning
intervals.note: No separate proposal, construction-start or commissioning date was found; only the approval date is sourced. The operating interval below is sourced to arXiv:2305.09383 / PRL 131, 031802.

end.note: Ends at the LHC-wide start of Long Shutdown 3 (June 2026); SND@LHC only detects particles from LHC collisions, so it cannot be active while the LHC is off.

intervals.label: data-taking (LHC Run 3)
intervals.note: The SND@LHC Collaboration's own first-neutrino-observation paper states it used 'a data set of proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13.6 TeV collected by SND@LHC in 2022'. This establishes SND@LHC as an operating, data-taking experiment from 2022. Year precision only; no exact first-data day or month is sourced.
intervals.quote: A data set of proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13.6 TeV collected by SND@LHC in 2022 is used, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 36.8 fb-1.

end.note: CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: SND@LHC detects neutrinos and other particles produced in LHC collisions, so it is idle while the LHC is shut down; this is an inference, since no SND@LHC-specific statement about this shutdown was found. Status is shutdown, not upgrade. The collaboration's home page (checked 2026-10-25) does not mention LS3 or an upgrade. No source consulted says that SND@LHC's own detector is being upgraded in LS3. Start and end are the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 dates. CERN's 5 August 2026 item says 'The cryogenics team has been running the warm-up sequence since LS3 began on 29 June 2026' and that the stored helium is kept 'ready to be used again once the accelerator resumes operation in mid-2030'; CERN's 29 June 2026 article says 'The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030'. The end is a schedule value, not a reported event.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

notes: The official SND@LHC site is snd-lhc.web.cern.ch (checked 2026-10-25); home.cern/science/experiments/snd-lhc returns 404 and sndlhc.web.cern.ch does not resolve (checked 2026-10-25).

key_specs pseudo-rapidity coverage value is left as a bare label with a null quantity because pseudo-rapidity_coverage is a sourced-string (S) Appendix-A key, not a quantity; the value '7.2 < eta < 8.6' is instead carried on physics_goals/unique_capabilities above with its quote.
The 2023 muon-neutrino-observation PRL is used only as timeline evidence for the 'active' interval; no results or technical documents are recorded for SND@LHC yet.

SND@LHC has taken Run 3 data since 2022: the collaboration's 2023 PRL (arXiv:2305.09383, 'Observation of Collider Muon Neutrinos with the SND@LHC Experiment', PRL 131, 031802) states data were collected 'in 2022'. SND@LHC cannot record anything while the LHC is off for LS3, so its status is shutdown.

physics_goals.quote: a hitherto unexplored pseudo-rapidity range of 7.2 < eta < 8.6 complementary to all the other experiments at the LHC, including FASER
physics_goals.value: Measure neutrinos produced in LHC pp collisions in an unexplored forward pseudo-rapidity range, complementary to FASER and the other LHC experiments

summary.plain: SND@LHC is a compact experiment in a disused CERN tunnel that catches neutrinos produced in LHC collisions, in a direction close to the beam that no other LHC experiment can see. It recorded collision data from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.
summary.technical: Stand-alone forward neutrino/long-lived-particle detector in the TI18 tunnel, covering the pseudo-rapidity range 7.2 < η < 8.6, complementary to FASER. Approved 17 March 2021; recorded LHC Run 3 pp-collision data from 2022 (arXiv:2305.09383) through June 2026; off since CERN's Long Shutdown 3 began.

unique_capabilities.quote: a hitherto unexplored pseudo-rapidity range of 7.2 < eta < 8.6
unique_capabilities.value: A compact, stand-alone detector covering a pseudo-rapidity range (7.2-8.6) not accessible to any other LHC experiment
